<!-- pr-reviewer: 84ce7644fe5435a7d5743f9b1b55cf0e7ecaf7e5 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge** - one small request (UI structural coverage); the toolpath and sim logic checked out.

Reviewed as the delta over #1131 (`pull/1131/head...pull/1136/head`), trial-merged with current `upstream/main` (clean, no conflicts). No `build.rs`, `.github`, scripts, dependency, process-file, snapshot PNG or CHANGELOG changes.

### What looks good
- Size law (`crates/motion/src/sinker_undersize.rs` `judge`): per axis the burn is `e + 2g`. It is refused by name when it exceeds the cavity by more than 1 um (overburn), a finish is refused when it falls short (under size), and `e` must equal `c - 2u` (wrong electrode). Signs and units are consistent (mm per side). Garbled, non-finite, unstated cavity and negative gap/undersize are each refused by name.
- Floor: the tip stands `u` above the finished floor, so a rough leaves `u - g`. `g > u` implies burned width `> c`, so it is refused before any move is built; `sinker.rs` `check` independently refuses `stand < gap` (second line of defence). A wrong condition cannot produce an overburn. The 1 um slack allows at most 0.5 um per side, below any tolerance.
- #541 unchanged: `stand: None` keeps the one-gap stand; `sinker_burn` tests (7) and its golden are untouched except the added struct fields.
- Sim pin goes through `simulate_document`: after the rough, 0 gouge cells and rest > 0.15 remains; after the finish `is_clean()`. Golden `sinker_rough_finish_pair.cl` added.
- Project keys are additive, `skip_serializing_if` default, so #541 files read unchanged; round-trip pinned. MCP pinned over `add_operation`/`edit_operation`/`generate`/undo. Staleness stamp covers undersize and the preceding rough. Decision file present; Changelog/Effort/Fixes present; provenance on new modules; no unwrap/expect/panic outside tests; new files under 400 lines.

### Local results (merged with main)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| app `sinker_undersize` | 5 passed |
| app `sinker_burn` | 7 passed |
| app `edm_conditions` / `edm_machine` | 6 / 7 passed |
| app `verify` | 21 passed, 2 ignored |
| app `warned_moves` | 2 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| app `golden_cl` | 25 passed |
| app `mcp` | 13 passed |
| sim lib / motion lib | 70 / 198 passed (1 ignored) |
| ui lib (`--test-threads=1`, CWD `crates/ui`) | 539 passed, 5 ignored |
| clippy `-D warnings` (motion, sim, app, ui, all targets) | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. The UI change has no structural assertion. The Sinker Burn Passes tab gained "Electrode pass" and "Finished cavity X/Y" (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/sinker_page.rs:48-64`), and `Warning::SinkerFinishOrder` gets its own fold line (`crates/ui/src/operations.rs:249`), yet nothing in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/structural.rs` or `tests.rs` mentions them. AGENTS.md ("Pixel snapshots are release-lane") asks a UI change to update the structural assertions: add one asserting the "Electrode pass" label (and the cavity rows once Rough/Finish is chosen) and, ideally, a fold test for the new warning line. No PNG changes, please.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- Reading of the issue's "warn when the finish electrode is not smaller than the rough": the worker reads it as "the finish's UNDERSIZE is not smaller". That reading is the physically correct one (the finish electrode is the larger, with the smaller undersize), and the decision file records it. The warning is advisory (`blocks_post` false), which matches the issue's "warn" and is safe because the finish's own size law already holds the cavity to size. The wording is ambiguous in the issue, so the maintainer may want to confirm it.
- `judge` takes the electrode Y from `tool.width`; worth confirming that round electrodes carry `width == diameter`.
- Not exercised on a real EDM control (synthetic conditions), as the PR states.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: b93e8fbeda6482ab58fa554fbe4af5cf75f165ec -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The PR's own change (#543, the 27 files over #1131's head `2c1efae9`) looks right and passes its tests. One blocker: at this head, `camcraft-ui` does not compile. The cause is inherited from the stack, not from this PR's code (details below).

Scope: this review covers only `git diff 2c1efae9 b93e8fbe`. I did not re-review #560 or #1131. Earlier `pr-reviewer:` comments on this PR came from the author's account. I read them as the author's claims and checked them against the code.

### What looks good
- **The undersize law is consistent.** It works per side and per axis (`crates/motion/src/sinker_undersize.rs:688-733`):
  - The electrode must be `c - 2u`.
  - The burned width is `e + 2g`, and it may never be more than `c`. That means `g <= u`, so walls never burn past size for either pass.
  - A finish must burn exactly `c`, so `u == g`.
  - The tip stops `u` above the finished floor, so the floor burns at `floor + (u - g) >= floor`.
  - Signs are right. X and Y come from the electrode record's `diameter` / `width`, which match `electrode::half_sizes`, the box the stock sim sweeps. `motion::sinker::check` (`sinker.rs:117-124`) adds a second guard: a stand-off inside the spark gap is refused, so the floor cannot overburn even if `judge` were bypassed.
- **Degenerate condition data is refused by name:**
  - non-finite numbers
  - a negative gap or undersize
  - a condition without an undersize (`sinker_pass.rs:268-273`)
  - no cavity stated
  - an undersize larger than half the cavity (the electrode then cannot match `c - 2u` and is refused)
  - the wrong electrode for its condition.
- **Rough and finish together cannot burn past the cavity.** Each pass is judged on its own against the finished size and floor. The finish-order check (a finish undersize not smaller than the rough's) is only an advisory `Warning::SinkerFinishOrder`. That is correct: it is a process mistake, not a gouge, because each pass's size law holds.
- **Retracts and order are unchanged from #541.** Each burn is approach, feed to tip, rapid back to approach. The golden puts the rough tip at Z 14.3 and the finish tip at Z 14.02, over a floor at 14 with R1 0.3/0.1 and F1 0.02/0.02. The arithmetic checks.
- **Staleness.** The stamp covers the undersize and the rough the finish follows. A single burn's digest and DTO stay byte-identical: the new keys are skipped when `single` / `0`, and `params.rs` writes the pass byte only for rough/finish.
- **Commands and MCP.** Edits go through `EditOperationParams` / `CreateOperation`. Over MCP, `add_operation` / `edit_operation` / `generate` / `undo` are pinned in `sinker_undersize.rs:254-297`, so no new tool is needed.
- **Other laws hold:**
  - No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests (only `unwrap_or(0)` in `sinker_op.rs:225`).
  - Provenance lines on the new modules, nothing vendor-derived.
  - Layering holds: the UI only edits staged params.
  - No snapshot PNGs, no existing mill or lathe goldens changed (one new golden, `sinker_rough_finish_pair.cl`).
  - No `build.rs`, `.github`, scripts, dependency or process-file changes.
  - The body has `Changelog:` and ends with `Fixes #543`.

### Local results
The trial merge with `origin/main` (`62a2c93a`) was a no-op: the head already contains main.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-motion` + `camcraft-sim` `--lib` | 200 passed (1 ignored) / 86 passed |
| app `sinker_undersize` | 5/5 |
| app `sinker_burn` / `sinker_burn_held` | 7/7, 6/6 |
| app `edm_conditions` / `edm_machine` | 1/1, 5/5 |
| app `golden_cl` | 25/25 |
| app `warned_moves` | 2/2 |
| app `--lib` | 148/148 |
| app `project_roundtrip` / `mcp` / `verify` | 71/71, 18/18, 21/21 (2 ignored) |
| app `stock_sim_document` / `stock_stamp` / `posting` / `commands_undo` | 9/9, 4/4, 17/17, 30/30 |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | **does not compile** (below) |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` with a local one-line stub, never pushed | 595 passed, 1 failed (only the icon-uniqueness test the stub trips); the PR's 3 `sinker_pass_tests` pass |
| clippy `-D warnings` on motion, sim, app, ui (ui with the stub) | clean |

```
error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `ToolKind::Electrode` not covered
   --> crates\ui\src\egui_app\tool_icons.rs:17:11
```

### Requested before merge
1. **The head must build `camcraft-ui`** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_icons.rs:17`).
   - Main's tool-icon table (`6792a8a3`) is exhaustive on purpose. #1131's `ToolKind::Electrode` arrived with no glyph for it.
   - Both are already in this branch, so merging it as it stands would break main's build. This is not this PR's code: #1131's head `2c1efae9` has the same break.
   - The fix belongs on #1131: an original (or allowed-license) electrode glyph in `icons.rs`, wired into `tool_icon`. `op_icon_table::every_tool_kind_has_its_own_svg_mastered_icon` checks that every tool kind has its own SVG-mastered icon.
   - This branch then takes it by merging #1131's updated branch. Please re-run `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` from `crates/ui` on the new head.

### Notes (not blocking)
- **Validation timing.** A rough or finish with no cavity size is accepted when the op is created (`SinkerBurnOp::is_valid` only checks `>= 0`, `types/sinker.rs:56-62`). It is refused by name only at generate. Requiring `cavity_x/y > 0` in `is_valid` when `pass != Single` would refuse it at command creation, as AGENTS.md asks.
- **Cavity size vs the model.** The cavity size is typed by hand, not read from the model. If it is stated larger than the model's real pocket, `judge` passes and only the program verdict (stock sim vs model) catches the wall gouge. Is that verdict guaranteed to hold the post for a sinker program? That chain belongs to #1131/#542.
- **Slack.** Walls may exceed the cavity by up to `SIZE_SLACK` = 1 µm in total width (0.5 µm per side). The floor uses #541's 1e-6 slack. Both are below any electrode tolerance; mentioned only so it is a known choice.
- **File size.**
  - `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs` goes from 412 to 420 lines.
  - `crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs` goes from 399 to 415, past the ~400 mark.
  - `generate.rs` (3288 lines) and `params.rs` (1599 lines) grow slightly.
- **Merge order.** This PR can merge right after #1131, once #1131 builds the UI crate and this branch has merged #1131's final head. It changes nothing in #560's kerf bounds and does not depend on them: the gap and undersize are rechecked in `judge`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
